author: product-requirements-expert
title: Correct a booked visit's date and description
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected. Opening its form shows the current values; a valid submission updates that visit in place without adding another visit to the pet and returns to the owner's record; an invalid submission is refused with the offending field named.
acceptance_criteria: The correction form for a booked visit is shown filled with that visit's current date and description
A valid correction (non-blank description, date later than today) updates that visit and shows the owner's record
A valid correction leaves the pet with no additional visit; the same visit carries the amended values
A blank description is refused and the correction form is redisplayed with the description named
A date of today or earlier is refused and the correction form is redisplayed with the date named

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Visit correction is the existing edit-in-place form-controller pattern applied to Visit. It reuses the pattern PetController already realizes for pet edit (system-design.md Contracts row for PetController; State Machine section: 'the pet workflows branch on isNew to choose between insert and update'). No new module, pattern, dependency, or ADR. The non-goal ADR (2026-08-05-non-goal-visit-amendment.md) already frames the split; its README index row is added on this dispatch. IDE oracle not available on this dispatch (no search_symbol/get_symbol_info tools granted) — resolution claims below verified by direct Read of the source, the weaker basis than an oracle citation.
integration_points: Add GET/POST mappings for /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit to VisitController, alongside the existing /visits/new pair.

Form has no th:action and posts to the current URL, so the shared createOrUpdateVisitForm template posts back to the /edit URL with no action change needed; id binding stays disallowed via the existing @InitBinder (setDisallowedFields id, *.id), so the visitId comes from the path, not the form.
On success, save the owner (owners.save) and redirect:/owners/{ownerId} — the same terminal redirect the new-visit flow uses; do NOT call owner.addVisit / pet.addVisit on the edit path.

patterns.description: @ModelAttribute('pet') findPet branches on petId: null -> new Pet(), else owner.getPet(petId) returns the EXISTING managed entity. The visit model attribute must mirror this: for the edit path return the existing managed Visit, not a fresh one.

updatePetDetails fetches the existing managed entity and mutates its fields, then saveAndFlush — a cascade UPDATE, not an INSERT. The visit edit path relies on the same mechanic: mutate the existing managed Visit (binding overlays date/description) and save the owner so JPA cascades an UPDATE to the existing visit row.

risks.risk: Duplicate-visit / 'pet gains an additional visit'. The current @ModelAttribute('visit') loadPetWithVisit unconditionally does `new Visit(); pet.addVisit(visit)` and runs before EVERY @RequestMapping method in the controller. If the edit mappings are added without branching this method, every edit GET and POST attaches a phantom empty Visit to the pet; on POST the @Valid 'visit' param resolves to that fresh instance and owners.save cascades an INSERT — the pet gains an extra visit. This is the load-bearing failure the PRD's 'must not gain an additional visit' criterion guards.
risks.mitigation: Branch @ModelAttribute('visit') on an optional visitId path variable exactly as PetController.findPet branches on petId. When visitId is present, look up the existing Visit within pet.getVisits() by id and return that managed instance WITHOUT adding a new one; when absent, keep today's new-visit behavior. Pet has no getVisit(id) — either add a private finder in VisitController iterating pet.getVisits(), or add a domain finder Pet.getVisit(Integer id) mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer id) (Owner.java:117) for symmetry (Pet.java in supporting_paths if chosen). Binding then mutates that managed Visit in place; saving the owner cascades an UPDATE.

risks.risk: Non-future-date validation must be reproduced on the edit POST. The @Valid @NotBlank on Visit.description covers the blank-description rejection, but the 'date later than today' rule is enforced imperatively in processNewVisitForm (result.rejectValue on date), not by an annotation.
risks.mitigation: Repeat the same date check on the edit POST before result.hasErrors(); reuse the existing 'typeMismatch.visitDate' error code and the minVisitDate model attribute the template already reads. On any error return 'pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm' to redisplay, matching processNewVisitForm.

notes: Template createOrUpdateVisitForm.html: for an existing (non-new) visit, visit['new'] is false, so the heading renders 'Visit' (not 'New Visit') and the Previous Visits table becomes visible — acceptable for reuse. The Add-Visit button label (#{addVisit}) is a presentation detail the implementer may refine but no design change requires it. Doc-sync follow-up (post-implementation, not a triage write): the system-design.md Contracts VisitController row description and its Implements column should gain REQ-VIS-003 once the flow lands.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: IDOR prevented: visit resolved by containment (owner.getPet(petId) then pet.getVisit(visitId) over that pet's visits only); a crafted URL naming another pet or owner returns null and throws, with no global id lookup

Mass assignment blocked: controller-wide @InitBinder setDisallowedFields id and *.id governs the edit binding; Visit exposes only date/description with no bindable pet reference, so identifiers cannot be rebound and the visit cannot be reassigned

Missing-visit path fails safe: IllegalArgumentException message carries only integer path values (petId/visitId are int/Integer, non-numeric fails path binding first); no sensitive detail or XSS reaches the REQ-SYS-002 error page, consistent with existing owner/pet not-found messages
No new endpoint surface beyond the declared /edit pair; Owner @ModelAttribute binding mirrors the pre-existing new-visit flow, not worsened versus baseline

author: code-quality-reviewer

findings.description: Pet.getVisit(Integer id) uses a single combined && condition rather than the nested-if-with-local-variable style used in Owner.getPet(Integer id) (verified by direct Read of Owner.java:117-127; IDE oracle not consulted). findings.fix: Replace 'if (!visit.isNew() && Objects.equals(visit.getId(), id))' with the nested form: 'if (!visit.isNew()) { Integer compId = visit.getId(); if (Objects.equals(compId, id)) { return visit; } }' to match Owner.getPet exactly.
